messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High tail latency detected on /v1/chat/stream (us-west-2). p95 rose from ~200ms to ~720ms; p99 peaked at 3.1s. Potential service: redwood-chat-7b-v2-serving. AlertID: 1876549999. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

alisa: taking pager. @sre-oncall @eng-runtime please standby. I'll collect live impact and start mitigation steps.

omar: grabbing decode & prefill logs now. Early tail traces show stalls at the decode step, while prefill completions dip. Example tail:
```
[2026-03-14T22:33:20Z] decode: node=decode-22 req=xyz789 stall_ms=1400 tokens_emitted=4
[2026-03-14T22:33:20Z] prefill: node=prefill-8 completed_ops=0 queue=5
```

maya: metrics: kv_cache_evictions_total 5m rate jumped x5. per-shard fragmentation_ratio up to 0.71 on several shards. Prefill throughput and hit ratio both dropped during the spike. Looks like high eviction + fragmentation turning cheap cache hits into full decodes.

pete: plausible root: allocator fragmentation leading to eviction storms. Long-lived sessions push many distinct keys then evict other working sets; prefill bursts then immediate evictions = chasing. Also saw some large single-request TTL resets.

jon: customer impact: SYN-ENT-02 and SYN-ENT-09 on our enterprise list reported streaming stalls in staging/production. CX ticket: #5310, #5313. No content errors, only degraded latency/timeouts.

ingrid: proposed immediate actions: A) add temporary route-level fallback to a smaller model variant for heavy sessions, B) increase decode worker capacity to drain backlog, C) reduce prefill concurrency to lower eviction churn, D) run targeted compaction on the most fragmented kv shards. Which do we run first?

alisa: run A and B in parallel. I'll apply a fallback to redwood-chat-4b-compat for sessions with continuous token rate >50 tokens/min. Pushing patch now:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.internal/routes/chat-stream -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"session_fallback":{"model":"redwood-chat-4b-compat","trigger_tokens_per_min":50,"duration_s":1800}}'
```
Applied. Rolling to 10% routes, will ramp if helpful.

ingrid: scaling decode pool: `rictl scale pool decode-pool --region=us-west-2 --delta=+20%` 0s ago. Monitoring queue lengths.

omar: also pushing a short-term prefill throttle to reduce simultaneous prefill per shard to 18 and increase prefill_timeout to 1500ms to prevent runaway prefill overloads:
```yaml
runtime.prefill:
  max_inflight_per_shard: 18
  prefill_timeout_ms: 1500
```
Pushed via config-service.

maya: starting sequential restart of kv-cache pods for the three worst shards (shard-5, shard-9, shard-12) to force compaction. Doing one-at-a-time with 45s gap. Using: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache -n prod -l shard in (5,9,12)`

cassie-bot: synthetic load job started: small prompts and long continuous sessions to validate. Job ID: synth-1876549999-1.

sre-oncall: watching traces and SLOs. After initial mitigations p95 improved to ~260ms, p99 down to ~870ms for short prompts; long-session p99 ~1.4s. Keep rolling.

pete: check node metrics for memory fragmentation; `node_memory_Active_bytes` didn't spike, but the allocator free list fragmentation metric did. This explains large-scale evictions without total memory pressure. We should consider compaction/defrag and allocator tuning.

omar: noticed eviction spikes coincide with large prompt sessions that have many unique keys. Those sessions bypassed our per-session key cap. Temporarily enforcing `max_session_kv_keys=1024` for heavy sessions to limit churn. Pushing config now.

maya: first kv shard restart completed: fragmentation ratio reduced 0.71 -> 0.25, eviction rate dropped 65% on that shard. Second shard rolling now.

alisa: fallback ramp to 30% across heavy sessions; telemetry shows those sessions p99 < 500ms on 4b variant. Customers notice improved streaming continuity.

jon: notified account owners at SYN-ENT-02 and SYN-ENT-09 with mitigation notes and asked them to validate. CX tickets updated.

ingrid: suggested follow-up alerts: add per-shard eviction rate alarm (threshold: 3x baseline in 5m), fragmentation ratio alert >0.5, and prefill-inflight spike alert. I'll file infra alerts.

sre-oncall: after compactions and throttles, SLO alert has cleared on dashboard. Current snapshot: p95=240ms, p99=540ms. Incident-bot mark: ALERT_RESOLVED candidate.

incident-bot: Alert 1876549999: RESOLVED at 1876550320. Summary: mitigations applied and p99 recovered from 3.1s -> ~540ms.

pete: post-incident followups for runtime/infra teams: - design allocator compaction (seg-aware) and add background compaction under load, - implement LRU segment-aware eviction, - add per-request KV-hit latency metric, - consider adaptive prefill backpressure based on eviction rate.

maya: action: create runbook section for targeted kv-shard restart & compaction procedure, include safe rollout cadence and SLO watch commands. I'll own the runbook doc.

omar: I'll add tracing spans at prefill->decode handoff to capture hit/miss/eviction cause per-request. Need to correlate with shard id.

alisa: assigning owners: maya -> runbook + compaction playbook; pete -> eviction policy design + proposal; ingrid -> alerting + autoscale policies; omar -> tracing and session-key cap enforcement. I'll draft the postmortem and schedule follow-up sync.

jon: adding customer-impact summary and action items to incident ticket. Scheduling customer sync tomorrow.

alisa: final: root cause = KV cache fragmentation leading to eviction storms; secondary factor = prefill vs decode throughput imbalance that amplified tail latency. Short-term mitigations: model fallback, decode scaling, prefill throttling, targeted kv shard compactions. Long-term: allocator/eviction improvements and better per-session controls. Handoff to @sre-oncall for overnight monitoring. :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: acknowledged. Monitoring p99 and per-shard eviction alerts for next 6 hours; will escalate if >2x baseline. Great work team. :clap:
